standard_prerequisites.name: The sheaf of meromorphic sections of an invertible module and the fact that the sections of the module are contained in the meromorphic ones, so that the defining formula makes sense
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at statement lines 6181-6186 and in the identification of the local situation at proof lines 6197-6199
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies the definition of the ideal of denominators and lets the proof pass to an affine chart where the bundle is trivial.

standard_prerequisites.name: A regular meromorphic section becomes, after shrinking, a quotient of two nonzerodivisors in the coordinate ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the whole statement to an elementary statement about a fraction a over b in a ring with a and b nonzerodivisors.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-coherence of a sheaf of ideals is checked on localizations, and the closed subset defined by a nonzerodivisor is nowhere dense in an integral or reduced setting
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives quasi-coherence from the localization computation and the nowhere dense support of the two cokernels.

core_obligations: Reduce to an affine chart with trivial bundle: the question is local, so assume the scheme is the spectrum of a ring A and the invertible module is the structure sheaf, and after shrinking write the regular meromorphic section as a quotient a over b with both a and b nonzerodivisors (proof lines 6196-6200).

Quasi-coherence: set I to be the set of elements x of A with x times a over b again in A, and show that the same description holds after localizing at any element f, which is the localization computation that proves quasi-coherence of the ideal (proof lines 6202-6210).

The final statement: the principal ideal generated by b is contained in I, so the closed subset where b vanishes contains the support of the cokernel of the first inclusion and is nowhere dense because b is a nonzerodivisor; the same argument applies to the cokernel of the second inclusion using that the image of b under multiplication by s is the ideal generated by a (proof lines 6211-6217).
proof_roadmap: Localize the statement to an affine chart with trivial bundle and a section given by a quotient of nonzerodivisors (proof lines 6196-6200).
Prove quasi-coherence by a localization computation and bound the supports of the two cokernels by the vanishing locus of the denominator, which is nowhere dense (proof lines 6202-6217).
difficulty_reason: The lemma defines the ideal of denominators of a regular meromorphic section and asserts that it is a quasi-coherent ideal whose two natural inclusions into the structure sheaf and into the line bundle have cokernels supported on nowhere dense closed subsets (statement lines 6172-6194). The counted proof reduces the statement to an affine chart with trivial bundle and a section equal to a quotient of two nonzerodivisors, proves quasi-coherence by an explicit localization computation, and then shows that the principal ideal generated by the denominator lies in the ideal of denominators, which bounds both supports by the vanishing locus of a nonzerodivisor and hence makes them nowhere dense (proof lines 6196-6217). It is H2: the reduction and both arguments are carried out in the counted span, with no independent research-level content.
